title: CHAPTER XVIII - OF OFFENCES RELATING TO DOCUMENTS AND TO PROPERTY MARKS
overview: This chapter studies IPC Sections 463-489E, including 477A and the repealed entries 478 and 480. It explains forgery and electronic records, counterfeit authentication, falsification of accounts, property marks and currency offences through provision-level references to BNS Sections 335-350 and 178-182. Read each correspondence with its elements, qualifications and changes in scope.
objectives: Apply the three false-document modes before concluding that forgery occurred.
Distinguish making, possessing and using a forged record, and identify special instrument categories.
Explain account falsification and the role of employment, wilfulness and intent to defraud.
Distinguish ownership marks, official marks and receptacle-content marks.
Recognise repealed IPC entries and the relocation of currency offences to BNS Chapter X.
Choose the correct BNS subsection and penalty while preserving statutory qualifications.
transition: These BNS provisions commenced on 1 July 2024 under S.O. 850(E), dated 23 February 2024. Determine the date and nature of the alleged conduct, the IPC repeal-and-savings provisions in BNS 358 and Article 20(1) of the Constitution; the date a complaint is filed alone does not decide the substantive law. BNS Chapter XVIII contains Sections 335-350, while currency-note counterparts are in Chapter X, Sections 178-182. Consolidation and expanded coverage mean that a crosswalk is not a declaration of identical wording or liability.

groups.title: Forgery: definitions, documents and use
groups.explanation: Begin with the false-document test in BNS 335, then establish the prohibited intent in 336(1). Distinguish ordinary forgery, special classes of instruments, special purposes and knowing use. Electronic records are expressly covered. A false factual claim is not automatically a false document in the statutory sense.

groups.title: Counterfeit authentication and falsification of accounts
groups.explanation: Separate making a forgery from making or possessing counterfeit authentication tools, possessing a specified forged instrument, destroying protected instruments and employee account falsification. The intended forgery and document category determine the correct provision. BNS 341(3) adds a knowing-possession branch carrying up to three years and fine; 341(4) punishes knowing fraudulent or dishonest use as if the seal or instrument had been made or counterfeited.

groups.title: Property and other marks
groups.explanation: A property mark identifies ownership of movable property; a receptacle mark may instead mislead about contents or quality. Read the express defences and mental elements. Preserve the repealed IPC entries for continuity without treating old trade-mark provisions as operative BNS offences.

groups.title: Currency-notes and bank-notes
groups.explanation: These IPC Chapter XVIII offences now correspond to BNS Chapter X, not BNS Chapter XVIII. BNS 178-181 consolidate currency, coin and Government revenue-stamp offences. Separate counterfeiting, trafficking or use, knowing possession with intended use, and instruments or materials. BNS 182 retains a distinct resemblance-document regime.

keyPoints: False statement, false document and forgery are different questions: apply BNS 335 and then 336.
Special document categories in 337 and 338 affect both forgery and related possession or use offences.
BNS 340(2) punishes knowing fraudulent or dishonest use as if the user forged the document.
BNS 339 has a seven-year alternative for possession of a 338-type document; do not substitute the ten-year alternative in 338.
BNS 344 requires the specified employment capacity and wilful intent to defraud.
IPC 478 and 480 were repealed before BNS and have no direct operative counterpart here.
Property marks concern ownership; marks under 350 concern misleading contents or quality.
BNS 349: the precautions and information conditions are cumulative within that defence; otherwise acting innocently is an alternative.
Currency offences move to BNS Chapter X. Knowledge and intended use matter in 180, alongside its lawful-source explanation.
BNS 182 fines are up to Rs 300 and Rs 600 in the respective branches.
examFocus: Use this sequence: identify the date and applicable law; classify the document, mark or currency item; identify the act and its statutory mode; establish knowledge, dishonesty, fraud or specific intention; examine statutory qualifications; select the precise subsection; then state the authorised punishment. In comparison answers distinguish consolidation, expansion, relocation and prior repeal. Do not infer a criminal offence solely from a civil ownership dispute, inaccurate accounting entry or innocent receipt of currency.

practice.question: A genuinely executed deed contains a disputed ownership assertion. Is that alone forgery?
practice.answer: No automatic conclusion follows. Identify a false-document mode under 335 and the intent required by 336(1). A false assertion alone is not a substitute for those elements. Other offences, if alleged, need independent proof.

practice.question: A person knowingly submits a forged will as genuine with dishonest intent. Which provisions guide the analysis?
practice.answer: BNS 340(2) governs use; 338 identifies the special instrument category and the punishment as if the user forged it. Mere use must be distinguished from knowing dishonest or fraudulent use.

practice.question: Compare making a forged valuable security with possessing it intending fraudulent use.
practice.answer: Making falls under 338: life or up to ten years and fine. Knowing possession with the required intent falls under 339: life or up to seven years and fine. The conduct and alternative maximum differ.

practice.question: An employee corrects an accounting error openly and honestly. Does every alteration attract 344?
practice.answer: No. The specified employment connection, wilfulness and intent to defraud must be proved. An honest correction does not by itself satisfy those requirements.

practice.question: Should IPC 478 and 480 be assigned BNS property-mark numbers?
practice.answer: No. They were repealed before BNS. Preserve their historical entries and explain the separate trade-mark regime rather than inventing operative counterparts.

practice.question: What must a seller establish under the first defence in BNS 349?
practice.answer: Both reasonable precautions and no reason to suspect the mark, and the available supplier information when properly demanded. The alternative branch permits proof that the seller otherwise acted innocently.

practice.question: A person unknowingly receives a counterfeit note in ordinary change. Is possession alone sufficient under 180?
practice.answer: No. Knowledge or reason to believe and intent to use as genuine or let it be so used are required. Also consider the express explanation where possession from a lawful source is established.

practice.question: Where are IPC 489A-489E located in BNS, and is resemblance the same as counterfeiting?
practice.answer: Their subject matter corresponds to 178-182 in Chapter X. Section 182 is a distinct resemblance-document regime with fine-based branches and a rebuttable presumption; do not automatically substitute the counterfeiting offence in 178.
